items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...I don’t think he has the innate ability to be the next Bill Evans or that kind of thing.

ctx.x: My manager is the cell phone in my pocket which I hope I turned off. But yeah, people call and I have enough work to keep me happy. I guess that’s a good place to be, where you have enough steady work to continually to do something seven days a week if you want to, but not so much work that your life is dictated by your fame. I’m not famous. I’m in a type of music that is not popular music. So that’s fine with me.

I have a student who is a very good piano player in high school. And I struggle with advising him. He wants to go into music. Now I don’t think he has the innate ability to be the next Bill Evans or that kind of thing. But I think he could make a living in the music business. And I guess I’m not sure what to tell him. Do you have advice for young musicians, how to get ahead?

What’s motivating him to play right now? I mean if someone has, I mean some musicians come from a place where they have stage mothers or fathers who will go on to be the next American Idol. And other kids, they can’t even help it, they just love to play so much that they’re naturally inclined to do it and they’re brave enough to pursue it and to have the attention span to do it for hours and hours a day. So I’m assuming he’s a young gentleman. If he has the interest in doing it all the time and is willing to give…
